newsitem.title: USA: Revco signs deal to buy Big B.
newsitem.headline: Revco signs deal to buy Big B.

text.p: Revco D.S. Inc said it has signed a definitive agreement to buy regional drugstore chain Big B Inc for $380 million in cash, or $17.25 per share.
The agreement marks a $2.25 per share premium over an unsolicited offer that Revco made for Big B last month. Big B had rejected that offer as financially inadequate.
The companies said Big B's board of directors unanimously approved the $17.25 offer and recommends that Big B shareholders tender their shares.
Revco said it expects the transaction to be accretive to earnings in the first year of the combination.
Revco also said it will extend its tender offer for Big B shares until Nov 15. The offer had been set to expire at 1700 EST Monday.
The companies said the tender offer will be amended to relect terms and conditions contained in the merger agreement.
They also said all litigation between the companies will be withdrawn.

The agreement came after a weekend meeting of Big B's board to consider bids for the regional drugstore chain. It was not immediately known if other bidders submitted offers, although Big B previously said it received indications of interest above the $15 per share first offered by Revco.

The sale of Big B marks the latest acquisition in the rapidly consolidating drugstore industry. Rite Aid Corp signed an agreement this month to buy West Coast chain Thrifty PayLess Inc for $1.4 billion and Thrift Drug Inc, a unit of J.C. Penney Co Inc, agreed in August to buy Fay's Inc for about $285 million.
Big B's stock recently had been trading at about $16 per share on views that the company will be sold for more than Revco's $15 per share offer.
Like many other regional drugstore chains, Big B is fighting problems that have accompanied the burgeoning clout of managed health care companies and huge discount retailers.
The Bessemer, Ala.-based chain has been hurt by deteriorating profit margins and sales and its earnings have disappointed Wall Street.
